correctness.rationale: For four generators, a kernel-sign orientation puts 0 in their tetrahedral convex hull. The Shephard determinant sum then equals one tetrahedral determinant, which is one quarter of the determinant of three balanced signed sums. Each signed sum has norm at most twice the circumradius. Equality in Hadamard and the three radial bounds is equivalent to three perpendicular signed sums of maximal norm. Inversion yields a common shift of a regular tetrahedral generator set. Exhausting all remaining signed half-sums gives 2||v||<=R and ||v-q_i||<=R; the convex-hull condition gives the four linear inequalities. The converse recomputes both the volume and circumradius. A strict open ball of nonzero shifts is feasible. The exact rational example with R=2 and v=(1/10,0,0) has volume 16 and unequal squared edge lengths 321/100 and 281/100. The embedded Python program replayed 4,000 exact-rational randomized checks, all sixteen signed sums, determinant identities and the witness. Finite checking is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The novel content assessed is the exhaustive necessary-and-sufficient equality locus for every 3-dimensional four-generator zonotope and its boundary, with a simple explicit ball-and-tetrahedron parameter region. The sharp volume/circumradius inequality, general zonotope volume identity, and small common-shift construction are NOT claimed new. The lead source proves the bound and states uniqueness as an open Problem 1; the source already uses common shifts in its separate fixed-mean-width analysis, so mere nonuniqueness would not qualify by itself. value.rationale: A sharp geometric isoperimetric-type bound is known but the complete class of minimizers and an explicit uniqueness problem were unsettled in the primary paper. The result proves a global equality classification with an explicit compact feasible region (four linear plus five quadratic conditions), not a narrow recalculation or a merely local perturbation. It exhibits a full-dimensional nonregular equality family and exactly delineates all permissible shifts, including degenerate boundary cases, making it useful for understanding rigidity/nonrigidity of extremal spatial zonotopes.
